steps.thought: I need to list all available tests to understand the station's testing capabilities and select the most efficient diagnostic path.

tests.name: power_on_selftest
tests.description: Boot the unit and enumerate devices on I2C, UART and CAN.

tests.name: battery_rest_check
tests.description: Read pack and per-cell voltages at rest.

tests.name: esc_telemetry
tests.description: Read ESC telemetry: sync errors, packet loss, back-EMF detection.

tests.name: compass_static
tests.description: Compare compass heading to the fixture reference with motors off.

tests.name: harness_continuity
tests.description: Measure per-bus continuity resistance and CAN termination.

tests.name: camera_selftest
tests.description: Run camera built-in self test and measure frame rate and CSI errors.

tests.name: imu_static
tests.description: Log 1000 IMU samples on the static fixture: gyro bias, accel noise, dropouts.

tests.name: motor_spin_test
tests.description: Spin all motors at 50 percent throttle: current, RPM, RPM jitter, temp.

tests.name: compass_motor_interference
tests.description: Sweep throttle 0-75 percent and log compass heading deviation.

tests.name: battery_load_test
tests.description: Apply a 20 A load and measure sag, cell imbalance, internal resistance.

steps.thought: I will run power_on_selftest as the cheapest initial system check to enumerate devices and verify basic subsystem health.
steps.observation: The power_on_selftest passed successfully, enumerating all expected CAN nodes, UART devices, camera sensor, I2C IMU, and compass. This rules out severe hardware connection failures during boot, but further subsystem-specific tests are required to check for degraded components.

hypotheses.rationale: Initial power on selftest passed with no failures across any bus.
Boot and enumeration passed, but ESC commutation issues might only appear under active motor spin tests.
I2C IMU was found during boot, but calibration and sensor noise require a static IMU check.
Camera sensor ID was read successfully during boot, but a CSI ribbon fault could cause frame loss under load.
Power-on passed, but battery under load needs verification.

steps.thought: I will run the battery_rest_check to verify individual cell voltages and pack condition as a quick, low-cost next step.
steps.observation: The battery_rest_check passed cleanly with a pack voltage of 16.593V, balanced cell voltages around 4.15V, and a very low cell imbalance of 0.007V, ruling out severe battery health issues at rest.

hypotheses.rationale: Both power-on self-test and battery rest checks have passed with zero failures.
Boot and battery passed, but ESC commutation issues require motor tests to verify.
I2C IMU was enumerated successfully, but static noise and calibration require testing.
Camera sensor ID read correctly, but CSI errors under self-test need confirmation.
Compass was detected during boot, but static or motor interference checks are still pending.

steps.thought: I will run the esc_telemetry test next to check for any commutation desyncs, packet loss, or back-EMF anomalies across the ESCs.
steps.observation: The esc_telemetry test passed successfully overall, showing 1 sync error on esc_4 with very low packet loss and normal temperatures across all ESCs, confirming no severe motor or ESC desync faults so far.

hypotheses.rationale: Power-on self-test, battery rest check, and ESC telemetry have all passed with no critical failures.
ESC 4 reported a single sync error, which warrants further motor spin testing to check for commutation issues.
IMU was detected at boot, but static performance and gyro calibration must be verified with an IMU test.
Camera sensor initialized successfully during boot, but selftest is needed to check for CSI packet drops.
Compass was enumerated properly on I2C, but static heading and magnetic interference tests remain pending.

steps.thought: I will run the imu_static test to check gyro bias, accelerometer noise, and dropouts, covering the IMU subsystem since the initial power-on self-test only verified enumeration.
steps.observation: The imu_static test passed with zero dropped samples, nominal gyro bias, and low accelerometer noise, ruling out IMU sensor faults and miscalibration.

hypotheses.rationale: Power-on, battery rest, ESC telemetry, and IMU static tests have all passed successfully with no significant anomalies.
ESC 4 previously reported 1 sync error, which should be investigated further with a motor spin test.
Compass was detected on I2C, but static heading and magnetic interference tests are still required.
Camera control and ID read successfully at boot, but camera selftest remains to be run.

steps.thought: Run compass_static to verify compass calibration and heading accuracy with motors off, as we need to test all subsystems before declaring the unit healthy.
steps.observation: The compass_static test passed successfully with a low heading error of 1.77 degrees and a field magnitude of 50.07 uT, ruling out severe static magnetic distortion or compass sensor issues.

hypotheses.rationale: Power-on, battery rest, ESC telemetry, IMU static, and compass static tests have all passed successfully with only minor, acceptable variations.
ESC 4 showed 1 sync error during esc_telemetry, which should be verified under load.
Compass static passed, but dynamic motor interference check has not been performed yet.

steps.thought: I will run the camera_selftest to check the camera subsystem, as we have not yet tested it.
steps.observation: The camera_selftest passed successfully with a nominal frame rate, OK sensor ID, and zero CSI CRC errors, ruling out camera sensor or ribbon cable faults.

hypotheses.rationale: All tests run so far (power_on_selftest, battery_rest_check, esc_telemetry, imu_static, compass_static, and camera_selftest) have passed successfully with only minor variations.
ESC 4 showed 1 sync error during esc_telemetry, which warrants further monitoring under motor load.

steps.thought: To check whether the single sync error on esc_4 indicates a developing motor or ESC issue under load, or if the unit is entirely healthy, I will run the motor_spin_test.
steps.observation: The motor_spin_test failed on motor_3 due to significantly elevated current (6.35 A), low RPM (7616), high RPM jitter (58), and high temperature (69.9 C), pointing directly to a mechanical or electrical issue on motor_3.

hypotheses.rationale: High current draw, high temperature, and significantly reduced RPM on motor_3 strongly suggest a partial winding short or inter-turn short.
Degraded bearings can increase mechanical friction, causing higher current draw, high temperature, and lower RPM on motor_3.
Demagnetized rotor magnets can cause reduced RPM and increased current draw under load.

steps.thought: Search the failure library for motor_3 current high, low RPM, and high temperature to distinguish between winding short, bearing degradation, and magnet demagnetization.

args.query: motor_3 current high rpm low temp high

matches.title: Motor rpm low with demagnetized rotor
matches.symptom_summary: One motor spins faster than the others at the same throttle with slightly higher current; back-EMF constant low. Temperature normal.
matches.root_cause: Rotor magnets partially demagnetized by overheating during an earlier burn-in.
matches.rework_notes: Replace the motor. Rare; check burn-in logs.

matches.title: Motor current high after propeller strike
matches.symptom_summary: One motor draws high current and runs hot after a drop at the previous station; rpm slightly low. Visible bent shaft.
matches.rework_notes: Historical variant of FL-002 caused by handling damage.

matches.title: Motor overheats with low rpm and very high current
matches.symptom_summary: One motor draws about 50 percent extra current, rpm drops well below spec, and temperature exceeds the 58 C limit. Burnt varnish smell after the spin test.
matches.root_cause: Turn-to-turn short in the stator winding from damaged insulation.
matches.rework_notes: Replace the motor. Low rpm plus overheating separates this from a bearing issue.

steps.observation: The motor_spin_test failed on motor_3 due to a high current draw of 6.35 A, low RPM of 7616, and high temperature of 69.9 C, matching historical failure records for a motor winding short.

hypotheses.rationale: High current, significantly reduced RPM, and excessive heating (69.9 C) strongly point to a turn-to-turn short in the stator winding.
Severe bearing friction could also cause high temperature and current draw, though less extreme RPM drop than a winding short.

steps.thought: I have identified the root cause as a motor winding short on motor_3 based on the motor_spin_test readings and failure library match. I will now propose the rework action to replace motor_3.
